Name: synthesizability_blindspot_steering
Title: The Synthesizability Tax: Do Interpretable Features Reveal That Property-Steering Silently Pushes Generators Toward Unmakeable Designs?
Short Hypothesis: When an interpretable feature is steered to improve a target property of a generated molecule, generation silently drifts toward LESS synthesizable chemical space, and this 'synthesizability tax' is systematic rather than random. We further hypothesize that molecular generative models do NOT possess a compact, causally-steerable internal feature encoding synthesizability itself (unlike easily-steerable physicochemical properties), so the manufacturability of a design cannot be controlled the way logP or QED can—making synthesizability an unrecognized interpretability blind spot for controllable design.
Related Work: Synthesizability is called 'the elephant in the lab' (Nature-adjacent opinion, 2025): generative models routinely propose molecules that cannot be made, and the field addresses this via post-hoc filtering (RAscore 2021, RetroGNN 2020), retrosynthesis-constrained generation (building-block assembly 2023, TANGO 2024, steerable synthesizability control 2025, SynTwins 2025), and direct retrosynthesis-in-the-loop optimization (2024). All of these are architecture/objective interventions treating synthesizability as an external constraint. Interpretability work on molecular generators—SynFlowNet interpretability (2025), 'Circuits, Features, and Heuristics in Molecular Transformers' (2025), token-level KL importance (2025)—shows physicochemical properties (polarity, lipophilicity, valence capacity) are linearly decodable and steerable, but NONE asks whether synthesizability is internally represented, whether it can be causally steered, or whether steering a DESIRED property incurs a hidden synthesizability cost. No prior work (a) quantifies a systematic property-vs-synthesizability tradeoff induced by interpretable-feature steering, (b) tests for the existence and causal steerability of an internal synthesizability feature, or (c) audits when a designer's property gain is silently paid for in unmakeability. This distinguishes the proposal from all constraint-based synthesizability work (which changes the model) and from all my prior steering proposals (which studied property control, memorization, provenance, chirality, symmetry, binding—never manufacturability).
Abstract: Generative molecular design has a notorious blind spot: models propose molecules that cannot be synthesized, the 'elephant in the lab.' The field fights this with retrosynthesis filters and synthesis-constrained generation, but no one has asked what happens to synthesizability when practitioners use the increasingly popular interpretable-feature steering to hit a target property. We surface and explain a behavioral phenomenon we call the synthesizability tax: steering an interpretable feature to improve a desired property (logP, QED, docking, a functional group) systematically drags generation into less synthesizable chemical space, and standard property-focused evaluations never see it. We then ask a mechanistic question: is synthesizability itself internally represented as a compact, causally-steerable feature—the way physicochemical properties demonstrably are—or is it an emergent, non-steerable global property that models cannot control? Using autoregressive SMILES chemical language models with sparse autoencoders and cheap synthesizability oracles (RAscore, SAscore, and a retrosynthesis-planner check on a subset), we (1) quantify the synthesizability tax across many property-steering features and its dose-response; (2) probe for and causally test an internal synthesizability direction (does steering it raise synthesizability while holding the graph's property fixed?); (3) audit per-design reliability, measuring how often a property gain is silently paid for by crossing a synthesizability cliff that validity checks and property predictors miss; and (4) test a mitigation—orthogonalizing property steering against the (weak) synthesizability direction. We predict a real, structured tax, a decodable-but-weakly-steerable synthesizability representation, and a cheap internal audit that flags unmakeable designs before expensive retrosynthesis.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Model: a GPT-style autoregressive SMILES chemical language model, either a public checkpoint (MolGPT, ~6M params) or one we train (~15M params, 8 layers, d=512) on ZINC-250k (249,455 drug-like molecules; 80/10/10 split). The base model is FROZEN throughout; we only add inference-time steering vectors. Interpretable directions come from TopK sparse autoencoders (SAE = a wide over-complete dictionary that reconstructs the residual stream with only the top-k latents active): expansion 16x, k=32, trained on 30M residual-stream activation vectors from a mid layer chosen by maximizing intrinsic dimension (one alternative layer kept for robustness), Adam lr 3e-4, batch 4096, seeds 0/1/2. Steering = add alpha*d_hat (unit direction d_hat) to the residual at that layer during decoding; alpha swept over {0,1,2,4,8,16} in units of residual-stream RMS. Oracles (all cheap, RDKit): logP, QED, molecular weight, ring count (PROPERTY targets); SAscore (0-10, higher=harder to make) and RAscore (0-1 synthesizable probability) as SYNTHESIZABILITY signals, validated on a 2,000-molecule random subset against AiZynthFinder route-found/not-found (proxy accepted iff |Spearman(SAscore, route-length)| >= 0.5). Validity gate: RDKit-parseable + valence-valid.

Experiment 1 (H1 - the synthesizability tax is systematic, not random): Tests that steering a property feature to raise a target property systematically lowers synthesizability. Data: ZINC held-out test set (24,945 molecules) to link features to properties; 30-50 property-steering features (top by property-probe AUROC) as the design knobs. For each (feature, alpha, seed) generate 500 valid molecules and measure the target-property gain and Delta-SAscore vs alpha=0. Systems: SAE-feature steering vs (a) random-direction control, (b) matched non-property SAE feature (equal activation norm, no property correlation). Decisive metric FIRST: the tax slope beta = d(SAscore)/d(target-property gain), from a mixed-effects model with random slopes over features and seeds. Decision band, stated before data: beta >= +0.30 SAscore units per +1.0 logP with 95% CI excluding 0 AND same-sign for >=80% of features => systematic tax confirmed; beta in [-0.10,+0.10] or CI crossing 0 => tax NOT established (null for H1's first clause); beta <= -0.10 => steering is synthesizability-SAFE, a clean positive counter-result refuting the tax.

Experiment 2 (H2 - the tax is a blind spot that standard output-side checks miss): Tests that the cheap checks a practitioner would actually run fail to reveal the synthesizability loss. Uses the already-labeled Experiment-1 generations. Detectors compared for flagging a 'synthesizability cliff' (RAscore crossing 0.5->below, or SAscore jump >=1.0): RDKit validity, the property-predictor's own confidence, generation log-likelihood. Decisive metric FIRST: Spearman rho between each output-side check and the true SAscore drop. Decision band: |rho| <= 0.20 for validity and property-confidence => blind spot confirmed (near-zero information about the tax); |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial visibility, report as such; |rho| >= 0.40 => NOT a blind spot, cheap checks already catch it (weakens the 'unrecognized' framing).

Experiment 3 (H3 - synthesizability is decodable but not compactly steerable, unlike logP/QED): Tests that synthesizability is linearly readable from activations yet cannot be causally dialed the way physicochemical properties can. Data: 20,000 held-out molecules labeled by SAscore/RAscore and logP/QED. (a) DECODABILITY: ridge linear probe (5-fold CV) for SAscore/RAscore from SAE features and raw activations; report R^2/AUROC. (b) STEERABILITY head-to-head in the same pipeline: take the best synthesizability direction (probe-weight, difference-of-means high-vs-low-SAscore, and activation-patching = copying activations from synthesizable runs) and the best logP and QED directions; steer each and measure the on-target effect size (Cohen's d of the oracle value, steered vs unsteered, at the alpha that maximizes on-target change within the validity budget), scaffold held fixed. Decisive metric FIRST: the steerability ratio r = d(synthesizability)/median(d(logP), d(QED)) at matched decodability. Decision band: probe R^2 >= 0.50 (decodable) AND r <= 0.33 across >=2/3 of direction types => H3 confirmed (decodable, not steerable); r in (0.33,0.67) => partial steerability, inconclusive; r >= 0.67 with a working direction => synthesizability IS a steerable handle, refuting H3 (equally useful and reportable). ROBUSTNESS (all three): repeat on SMILES vs SELFIES, the alternative SAE layer, and a 40M-param model; a finding 'counts' only where it holds on >=2 of these axes.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) SAscore/RAscore are in-silico proxies for true synthesizability; we validate them on a subset against an actual retrosynthesis planner (AiZynthFinder) and report proxy-vs-planner agreement, restricting strong claims to cases where they agree. Claims concern model-internal, proxy-verified manufacturability, not wet-lab synthesis. 2) The synthesizability-non-steerability claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching from high-synthesizability runs), sweeping strength, and head-to-head calibrating that PROPERTY features ARE steerable in the same pipeline—so a null synthesizability-steering result is meaningful rather than a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable synthesizability handle) is equally publishable and directly useful for controllable synthesis-aware design. 3) The tax could be confounded with generic off-distribution drift rather than a property-specific effect; we use random-direction and matched-non-property-feature controls and test whether the tax tracks property-specific displacement. 4) SAE quality/layer choice could confound both Location and the tax; controlled with multiple SAE variants, layers, and difference-of-means baselines. 5) An internal synthesizability probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; even so, the interpretability diagnosis (decodable-but-not-steerable) and the audit/mitigation payoff are the contributions, reported honestly. 6) If no tax is found (property steering leaves synthesizability intact), that is a valuable positive result establishing that interpretable steering is synthesizability-safe.

Name: regulatory_grammar_syntax_steering
Title: Motifs Without Grammar: Do Genomic Language Models Causally Steer Cis-Regulatory Syntax, or Just Sprinkle Motifs?
Short Hypothesis: Genomic language models (Evo 2 / regLM-style) possess interpretable, causally-steerable features for the PRESENCE of transcription-factor motifs, but NOT for their SYNTAX — the spacing, orientation, and ordering constraints that actually make a cis-regulatory element functional. Consequently, feature-steering to 'add motif X' silently places motifs in syntactically invalid configurations that break predicted regulatory activity, an unrecognized blind spot: activity/validity checks that look only at motif content miss it, while an intervention-free internal syntax-consistency signal flags it.
Related Work: Genomic interpretability is active but confined to motif PRESENCE. Evo 2 SAE work (2025) and small gene-LM SAE work (2025) discover features for coding sequences, TF-binding motifs, and secondary structure, and show early single-property steering. regLM (2024) and DREAM (2024) design CREs with target activity/cell-type-specificity via autoregressive LMs + supervised scorers, and ARGMINN (2024) makes motif SYNTAX (spacing preferences) readable from a purpose-built architecture. Critically: (a) all generative interpretability work steers toward motif content or scalar activity and evaluates whether the motif/activity appears — none asks whether the model represents motif SYNTAX as a causal, steerable handle; (b) ARGMINN reads syntax from weights but is a bespoke predictive model, not an audit of whether a general genomic LM causally controls syntax during generation; (c) benchmark critiques (DART-Eval 2024; gLM representational-power 2024; Karollus 2022 showing models ignore distal enhancers) hint that gLMs may capture correlational content over causal grammar, but never test this at the level of feature-steering controllability. This proposal is the first to introduce the content-vs-syntax axis into interpretability-of-generation for regulatory DNA and to audit when adding a motif silently violates grammar, distinct from all prior single-property CRE steering.
Abstract: The function of a cis-regulatory element (promoter, enhancer) is determined not just by which transcription-factor (TF) motifs it contains, but by their SYNTAX: the spacing, orientation, and order that let bound proteins cooperate. Interpretability-guided DNA design increasingly steers genomic language model (gLM) features to insert desired motifs, and success is judged by whether the motif appears and predicted activity rises. We surface a behavioral phenomenon we call the syntax blind spot: steering an interpretable feature to add a motif reliably increases motif content but places motifs in syntactically incoherent configurations that predicted-activity models score as non-functional — and content-based checks never notice. We then ask a mechanistic question: do gLMs represent motif syntax as a compact, causally-steerable feature the way they represent motif presence, or is syntax an emergent, non-steerable property? Using an open genomic LM (Evo 2 / a regLM-style autoregressive gLM) with sparse autoencoders and cheap in-silico oracles (FIMO/HMMER motif calling for content; a supervised sequence-to-activity model such as Enformer/DREAM for function; spacing/orientation statistics for syntax), we (1) LOCATE candidate motif-presence and motif-syntax features via probing; (2) CAUSALLY test whether steering each controls the intended axis — for syntax, whether we can shift inter-motif spacing/orientation while holding motif content fixed; (3) quantify the syntax tax that content-steering incurs on predicted activity; and (4) AUDIT design reliability, testing whether an internal syntax-consistency signal flags broken designs better than motif-content and activity-confidence checks. We predict content is steerable, syntax is decodable-but-weakly-steerable, and a cheap internal audit catches silently non-functional CREs before wet-lab validation.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models: (primary, affordable) a regLM-style autoregressive genomic language model, ~10M params, trained on the Vaishnav 2022 yeast random-promoter GPRA library (~20M measured sequences; subsample 1M for training, feasible on one GPU); (cross-model check) Evo 2 (7B, public) run FROZEN at its published biologically-relevant layer (~layer 26). Both base models FROZEN; only BatchTopK SAEs are trained (expansion 16x, k=32, 30M activations, seeds 0/1/2). Oracles: FIMO/JASPAR PWM motif calling (which TF motifs, at what positions) = CONTENT; inter-motif spacing, strand orientation, and 10.5-bp helical phasing = SYNTAX descriptors; a supervised sequence-to-activity model (the GPRA-trained CNN from Vaishnav 2022 for yeast promoters; Enformer for human) = FUNCTION oracle. Validity gate: GC-content bounds + gLM pseudo-perplexity. Data: 50,000 held-out yeast promoters to link features to properties; 5,000 controlled syntax-dissociation pairs (identical motif content, functional vs scrambled spacing) built by inserting motif pairs at controlled spacings. Steering = add alpha*d_hat at the SAE layer; alpha over {0,1,2,4,8} residual-RMS units.

Experiment 1 (H1 - motif-PRESENCE features are causally steerable): Identify presence features (fire when a given TF motif is present; kept if held-out probe AUROC >= 0.8) and steer to ADD a target motif to sequences that lack it. Generate 500 sequences per (feature, alpha, seed) for the 15 most frequent JASPAR yeast motifs. Systems: SAE-feature steering vs random-direction control. Decisive metric FIRST: motif-installation rate (FIMO detects the target motif within the validity budget). Decision band: installation rate >= 0.60 AND >= 0.40 above random control for >=2/3 of motifs => presence is a genuine handle (H1 holds); gain over control in [0.15,0.40) => weak, inconclusive; gain < 0.15 => presence NOT steerable, which undercuts the paper's premise (reported as such).

Experiment 2 (H2 - motif SYNTAX is decodable but NOT causally steerable): (a) DECODABILITY: probe SAE features/raw activations for syntax descriptors (spacing bin, relative orientation) controlling for motif content; report AUROC/R^2. (b) STEERABILITY head-to-head: attempt to shift inter-motif SPACING toward a target (e.g., 5 bp -> helically-phased 21 bp) while HOLDING motif content fixed, using the best syntax direction (SAE feature, difference-of-means functional-vs-scrambled-syntax, activation-patching from correct-syntax sequences). Decisive metric FIRST: syntax-steering efficacy ratio r = (normalized achieved spacing shift toward target)/(presence-installation efficacy from Experiment 1). Decision band: syntax decodable (AUROC >= 0.70) AND r <= 0.33 => H2 confirmed (readable but inert); r in (0.33,0.67) => partial, inconclusive; r >= 0.67 => syntax IS steerable, refuting H2.

Experiment 3 (H3 - steering 'add motif X' silently breaks syntax and predicted activity; content/validity checks miss it): Steer presence features and generate 500 sequences per level. Among content-satisfying, composition-valid, low-perplexity sequences, measure activity loss attributable to bad syntax. Decisive metric FIRST: SILENT-BREAKAGE RATE = fraction whose function-oracle activity falls below the 10th percentile of natural-CRE activity despite passing content+validity, plus Spearman rho between the cheap checks (content-satisfaction, pseudo-perplexity) and true activity. Decision band: silent-breakage rate >= 0.30 AND |rho| <= 0.20 => silent blind spot confirmed; breakage in [0.10,0.30) or |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial; breakage < 0.10 or |rho| >= 0.40 => not a silent blind spot (checks already reveal it).

Experiment 4 (H4 - an intervention-free internal syntax-consistency signal flags the silent failures): Build a no-intervention score = the syntax-probe's confidence / SAE-feature coherence read from activations mid-generation. Decisive metric FIRST: AUROC for detecting the eventually-non-functional (bad-syntax) sequences from Experiment 3. Systems: internal signal vs output-side detectors (content-satisfaction, pseudo-perplexity, function-oracle confidence). Decision band: internal AUROC >= 0.75 AND >= 0.10 above the best output-side detector => internal flag confirmed; margin in (0.05,0.10) => inconclusive; margin <= 0.05 => internal signal is no better (reported honestly; the decodable-not-steerable diagnosis still stands, the flag claim fails). ROBUSTNESS: repeat on Evo 2 vs regLM, promoter vs proximal-enhancer; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Both function and syntax are assessed by in-silico oracles (Enformer/DREAM/regLM scorers, FIMO/JASPAR); these are proxies for wet-lab regulatory activity, so claims concern model-internal, in-silico-verified syntactic controllability, not experimental function — stated explicitly. Sequence-to-activity models are known to capture promoters better than distal enhancers (Karollus 2022), so we focus core claims on promoter/proximal-enhancer regimes where the oracle is most reliable and report enhancer results separately. 2) The syntax-non-steerability claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching), sweeping strength, and head-to-head calibrating that PRESENCE features ARE steerable in the same pipeline — so a null syntax result is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable syntax handle) is equally publishable and valuable for grammar-aware CRE design. 3) Content and syntax may be irreducibly entangled for some motif combinations (identity implies canonical spacing); the controlled dissociation pairs (step 5) are designed to separate them and we report where separation is impossible. 4) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with multiple SAE variants, the Evo 2 published biologically-relevant layer, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 5) An internal syntax probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (content-decodable, syntax-weakly-steerable) and the audit payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 6) If no syntax tax is found (content steering preserves grammar and activity), that is a valuable positive result establishing that gLM feature-steering is grammar-safe for regulatory DNA design.

Name: rna_folding_mirage_steering
Title: The Folding Mirage: Do Interpretable Features Control an RNA's Local Motifs While Silently Breaking Its Global Thermodynamic Fold?
Short Hypothesis: Interpretable sparse-autoencoder features of RNA language models afford causal, steerable control over LOCAL structural motifs (a hairpin, a stem, a poly-U tract), but NOT over the GLOBAL thermodynamic fold that defines RNA function. Consequently, steering a feature to insert a desired local structure silently produces sequences whose true minimum-free-energy fold and target-structure Boltzmann probability collapse—a 'folding mirage'—that motif-content and validity checks miss, but which an intervention-free internal thermodynamic-consistency signal flags.
Related Work: RNA language model interpretability is nascent and purely descriptive: SAE-RNA (2025), SPIRAL/BiRNA-BERT (2026), and small gene-LM SAE work (2025) all find SAE features that localize to stems, hairpins, poly-G/C/A/U tracts and ncRNA families, but none steers generation or asks whether steering preserves the global fold. RNA design LMs (RNAinformer 2024; 'Designing RNAs with Language Models' 2026; AIDO.RNA inverse folding 2025) do supervised/RL inverse folding to hit a target secondary structure but offer no interpretability, no feature-level steering, and no audit of when control silently fails. Protein/molecule steering-audit work (InterPLM, ProtSAE, and my prior chirality/symmetry/syntax proposals) establishes the content-vs-global-property axis in other object classes but never in RNA. RNA is uniquely suited to this question because its defining functional property—the global fold—has an exact, instant, physics-grounded oracle (ViennaRNA MFE, partition function, and Boltzmann probability of any target structure), turning 'silent global failure' from a proxy into an objectively computable quantity. No prior work (a) causally steers RNA-LM features, (b) contrasts local-motif steerability against global-fold steerability, or (c) surfaces and audits the folding-mirage phenomenon. This is the first interpretability-of-generation study for RNA and the first to exploit RNA thermodynamics as a clean ground-truth oracle for steering reliability.
Abstract: An RNA molecule's function is determined by its global thermodynamic fold, not merely by which local motifs it contains: the same hairpin can be part of a functional structure or buried in a completely different minimum-free-energy conformation. Interpretability-guided sequence design increasingly steers language-model features to add desired structural elements, judged by whether the motif appears. We surface a behavioral phenomenon we call the folding mirage: steering an interpretable feature to insert a local structure (a hairpin, a stem) reliably increases that local motif's presence but drives the sequence's true global fold—its minimum-free-energy structure and the Boltzmann probability of the intended target—to collapse, a failure invisible to motif-content and validity checks. We then ask a mechanistic question: do RNA language models represent the global fold as a compact, causally-steerable feature the way they represent local motifs, or is global thermodynamic consistency emergent and non-steerable? RNA is the ideal testbed because ViennaRNA computes the exact global fold, ensemble free energy, and target-structure Boltzmann probability instantly and for free. Using RiNALMo/RNA-FM with sparse autoencoders, we (1) LOCATE candidate local-motif and global-fold features via probing; (2) CAUSALLY test the steerability of each, contrasting local-motif control against global-fold control; (3) quantify the mirage—the drop in target-structure Boltzmann probability that local-motif steering incurs; and (4) AUDIT reliability, testing whether an internal thermodynamic-consistency signal flags mirage sequences better than motif-content or model likelihood. We predict local control succeeds, global control is decodable-but-weakly-steerable, and a cheap internal audit catches silently misfolded designs.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models (public, FROZEN): RiNALMo (650M) and RNA-FM (~100M) RNA language models; being encoder models, generation is by masked infilling. Only SAEs are trained: TopK and Ordered SAEs (Ordered latents ranked by importance, the antibody-SAE recipe that can recover steerability TopK lacks), expansion 16x, k=32, 30M residual-stream activations at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer, seeds 0/1/2. Oracle (exact, cheap): ViennaRNA - RNAfold for the minimum-free-energy (MFE) structure and free energy, the partition function for ensemble free energy, and the Boltzmann probability that a sequence folds into a specified TARGET structure (the primary GLOBAL-fold signal). LOCAL-motif oracle: presence/position of a hairpin loop / stem / poly-U tract from the predicted structure. Validity gate: GC-content bounds + RNA-LM pseudo-perplexity. Data: 20,000 held-out ncRNA from Rfam spanning tRNA-scale (~76 nt) and longer families, to link features to properties; 5,000 controlled dissociation pairs (same local hairpin embedded in well-folded vs misfolded global context). Steering = add alpha*d_hat during masked infilling; alpha over {0,1,2,4,8}.

Experiment 1 (H1 - local-structural-motif features are causally steerable): Identify local-motif features (fire on a specific hairpin/stem/tract; probe AUROC >= 0.8) and steer to INSERT a target local motif. Generate 500 infilled sequences per (feature, alpha, seed). Systems: SAE-feature steering vs random-direction control. Decisive metric FIRST: local-motif installation rate (target motif appears in the RNAfold structure). Decision band: rate >= 0.60 AND >= 0.40 over control for >=2/3 of motifs => local control is genuine (H1 holds); gain in [0.15,0.40) => inconclusive; gain < 0.15 => local motifs not steerable (premise fails, reported).

Experiment 2 (H2 - the global thermodynamic fold is decodable but not steerable): (a) DECODABILITY: probe for global properties (MFE per nucleotide, ensemble free energy, base-pairing fraction, global fold class) controlling for local content; AUROC/R^2. (b) STEERABILITY head-to-head: steer the best global-fold direction (SAE feature, difference-of-means well-folded-vs-misfolded, activation-patching from correctly-folded sequences) to RAISE the target-structure Boltzmann probability while HOLDING local content fixed. Decisive metric FIRST: ratio r = global-fold steering efficacy / local-motif efficacy from Experiment 1. Decision band: global decodable (R^2 >= 0.40 or AUROC >= 0.70) AND r <= 0.33 => H2 confirmed; r in (0.33,0.67) => partial (test whether Ordered SAEs move it above 0.33); r >= 0.67 => global fold IS steerable, refuting H2.

Experiment 3 (H3 - the folding mirage: local steering silently collapses the global fold; motif/validity checks miss it): Steer local-motif features and generate 500 sequences per level. Decisive metric FIRST: SILENT-MISFOLD RATE = fraction of local-motif-satisfying, valid sequences whose target-structure Boltzmann probability < 0.10 (thermodynamically wrong), plus the mirage slope d(Boltzmann prob)/d(local-motif gain) and Spearman rho between cheap checks (motif-content, pseudo-perplexity) and true global-fold health. Decision band: misfold rate >= 0.30 AND |rho| <= 0.20 => mirage + blind spot confirmed; misfold in [0.10,0.30) or |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial; misfold < 0.10 or |rho| >= 0.40 => no silent mirage (RNA-LM steering is thermodynamically safe, a positive result).

Experiment 4 (H4 - an intervention-free internal thermodynamic-consistency signal flags the mirage): No-intervention score = global-fold-probe confidence / SAE-feature coherence read mid-generation. Decisive metric FIRST: AUROC detecting the misfolded (low-Boltzmann) sequences from Experiment 3. Systems: internal signal vs output-side (motif content, pseudo-perplexity, model likelihood). Decision band: internal AUROC >= 0.75 AND >= 0.10 over the best output-side detector => flag confirmed; margin (0.05,0.10) => inconclusive; margin <= 0.05 => no better (reported honestly). ROBUSTNESS: RiNALMo vs RNA-FM, short vs longer ncRNA, TopK vs Ordered SAEs; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Global fold is assessed by ViennaRNA (nearest-neighbor thermodynamic model), which is a well-validated but still in-silico oracle for secondary structure; it ignores tertiary interactions/pseudoknots and cellular context, so claims concern thermodynamic-model-verified global folding, not wet-lab function—stated explicitly. We can corroborate a subset with a structure-aware model (ERNIE-RNA/structRFM) and report agreement. 2) The global-fold-non-steerability claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (TopK and Ordered SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching), sweeping strength, and head-to-head calibrating that LOCAL-motif features ARE steerable in the same pipeline—so a null global result is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable global-fold handle) is equally publishable and directly useful for structure-aware RNA design. 3) The mirage could be confounded with generic off-distribution drift; we use random-direction and matched-non-motif-feature controls and test whether the mirage tracks motif-specific displacement. 4) Local and global structure are partly entangled (a large motif dominates the fold); the controlled dissociation pairs (step 5) separate them and we report where separation is impossible. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 6) An internal consistency probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (local-decodable, global-weakly-steerable) and the audit payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 7) If no mirage is found (local steering preserves global folds), that is a valuable positive result establishing that RNA-LM feature steering is thermodynamically safe.

Name: conservation_law_mirage_reactions
Title: Balanced by Habit, Not by Law: Do Reaction Generative Models Internally Represent Mass Conservation as a Steerable Feature, or Fake It?
Short Hypothesis: Autoregressive reaction-prediction models produce atom-balanced reactions (reactants and products with matching element counts) not because they possess a compact, causally-steerable internal representation of the conservation LAW, but via a shallow atom-copying heuristic tied to local token context. Consequently, steering an interpretable feature to alter a product's chemistry (add/remove an atom or functional group) silently breaks mass balance—a 'conservation mirage'—that ordinary SMILES-validity checks miss, while an intervention-free internal balance-consistency signal flags it. We further hypothesize there is no compact steerable 'atom-balance' feature the way there are steerable chemistry features, making conservation an unrecognized interpretability blind spot.
Related Work: FlowER (2025) and atom-conserving CRNNs (2023) show data-driven reaction models routinely VIOLATE mass/atom conservation, producing 'hallucinatory' unbalanced reactions, and fix this ARCHITECTURALLY by hard-coding electron/atom-balance layers—treating conservation as an external constraint, never asking whether a standard model internally represents it. 'Circuits, Features, and Heuristics in Molecular Transformers' (2025) finds molecular transformers implement ring/branch SYNTAX circuits and a steerable valence-capacity direction, and 'Physics Steering' (2025) shows physics foundation models have steerable concept directions—but neither studies reactions or the conservation invariant, and neither asks whether a global conservation law (as opposed to a local property) is a steerable handle. Conservation-law discovery work (Noether-from-DNN 2021; stoichiometry-nullspace methods 2014/2024) extracts laws from PREDICTIVE dynamics models, never from a generative reaction LM's internal features, and never tests steering reliability. No prior work (a) asks whether a generative reaction model represents mass/atom conservation as a causal, steerable feature, (b) surfaces the conservation-mirage phenomenon where chemistry-steering silently unbalances a reaction, or (c) provides an internal balance-reliability audit. This introduces the content-vs-conservation-law axis into interpretability-of-generation for chemical reactions—a new object class where conservation is an exact, instantly computable oracle (element-count matching / stoichiometry null space)—distinct from all prior single-property steering and from all architectural conservation fixes.
Abstract: Mass conservation is the most basic law of chemistry: a valid reaction has identical element counts on both sides. Yet data-driven reaction models are known to hallucinate unbalanced reactions, and the field fixes this by hard-coding balance into the architecture—never asking whether a standard model actually understands conservation internally. We surface and explain a behavioral phenomenon we call the conservation mirage. Autoregressive reaction-prediction transformers produce mostly balanced reactions, but we hypothesize they do so via a shallow atom-copying heuristic rather than a genuine internal conservation law: steering an interpretable feature to change a product's chemistry (add a methyl, swap a halogen, remove an oxygen) reliably changes the chemistry but silently breaks atom balance, a failure invisible to SMILES-validity checks and evident only from element counting. We then ask a mechanistic question: is mass/atom conservation represented as a compact, causally-steerable feature—the way local chemistry features demonstrably are—or is it emergent and non-steerable? Reactions are the ideal testbed because conservation is an exact, free oracle: element-count vectors (and the stoichiometry null space) instantly certify balance. Using an autoregressive reaction transformer trained on USPTO reactions with sparse autoencoders, we (1) LOCATE candidate chemistry features and candidate conservation features via probing; (2) CAUSALLY test the steerability of each, contrasting local-chemistry control against atom-balance control; (3) quantify the mirage—the balance-breakage that chemistry-steering incurs; and (4) AUDIT reliability, testing whether an internal balance-consistency signal flags unbalanced designs better than validity or model likelihood. We predict chemistry is steerable, conservation is decodable-but-weakly-steerable, and a cheap internal audit catches silently unbalanced reactions before wet-lab or DFT screening.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Model: an autoregressive reaction transformer (Molecular-Transformer-style, ~30M params) trained on USPTO-MIT reaction SMILES (479,035 reactions), filtered to the atom-balanced subset with atom-mapping retained; FROZEN after training. Only SAEs are trained: TopK and Ordered/Matryoshka SAEs (Ordered can recover steerability that TopK's decodable-but-inert features lack), expansion 16x, k=32, 30M residual-stream activations at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen mid layer, seeds 0/1/2. Oracle (exact, free via RDKit): the reactant-minus-product element-count residual - a reaction is atom-balanced iff the residual is the zero vector (charge balance and atom-mapping completeness also computed). LOCAL-CHEMISTRY oracle: presence/absence of specified product functional groups/atoms via SMARTS. Validity gate: RDKit-parseable, valence-valid on both sides. BASELINE (needed for the absence claim): confirm the frozen model natively emits atom-balanced products at rate >= 0.80 on held-out reactants, well above a token-shuffle chance rate; if it does not, the mechanism claim is reframed. Steering = add alpha*d_hat during product decoding given fixed reactants; alpha over {0,1,2,4,8}.

Experiment 1 (H1 - local-chemistry features are causally steerable): Identify chemistry features (fire when a product contains a given functional group/atom; probe AUROC >= 0.8) and steer to add/remove that group in the product given fixed reactants. Generate 500 completions per (feature, alpha, seed). Systems: SAE-feature steering vs random-direction control. Decisive metric FIRST: chemistry-installation rate (intended group/atom change appears in the product). Decision band: rate >= 0.60 AND >= 0.40 over control for >=2/3 of groups => chemistry control genuine (H1 holds); gain [0.15,0.40) => inconclusive; gain < 0.15 => chemistry not steerable (premise fails).

Experiment 2 (H2 - the conservation mirage: chemistry steering silently breaks mass balance; SMILES-validity checks miss it): Steer chemistry features and generate 500 completions per level. Decisive metric FIRST: SILENT-IMBALANCE RATE = fraction of chemistry-satisfying, SMILES-valid reactions whose element-count residual is nonzero, plus the mirage slope d(|residual|)/d(chemistry gain) and Spearman rho between cheap checks (SMILES-validity, pseudo-perplexity) and true balance. Decision band: imbalance rate >= 0.30 AND |rho| <= 0.20 => mirage + blind spot confirmed; imbalance [0.10,0.30) or |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial; imbalance < 0.10 or |rho| >= 0.40 => steering is conservation-safe (positive result).

Experiment 3 (H3 - conservation is decodable-but-not-steerable and rests on a shallow atom-copying heuristic, not a compact conservation-LAW feature): (a) DECODABILITY: probe 'is-balanced' / the element residual from activations, reporting AUROC and the earliest product-decoding position at which balance status is decodable. (b) STEERABILITY head-to-head: steer the best conservation direction (SAE feature, difference-of-means balanced-vs-unbalanced, activation-patching from balanced runs) to RESTORE balance (drive residual->0) while holding product chemistry fixed; ratio r = conservation efficacy / chemistry efficacy from Experiment 1. (c) MECHANISM (heuristic vs law): using the 4,000 controlled pairs that hold the same product functional group in balanced vs deliberately unbalanced reactions, test whether the located 'conservation' unit tracks the GLOBAL residual (law) or LOCAL product content (heuristic). Decisive metric FIRST: r, read together with the mechanism contrast. Decision band: r <= 0.33 AND the unit predicts local content (AUROC >= 0.80) but the global residual only at <= 0.60 => H3 confirmed (inert + shallow heuristic); r in (0.33,0.67) or residual-AUROC in (0.60,0.75) => partial; r >= 0.67 => a genuine steerable conservation handle exists, refuting H3.

Experiment 4 (H4 - an intervention-free internal balance-consistency signal flags the mirage): No-intervention score = conservation-probe confidence / SAE-feature coherence read mid-generation. Decisive metric FIRST: AUROC detecting the mass-unbalanced reactions from Experiment 2. Systems: internal signal vs output-side (SMILES-validity, pseudo-perplexity, model likelihood). Decision band: internal AUROC >= 0.75 AND >= 0.10 over the best output-side detector => flag confirmed; margin (0.05,0.10) => inconclusive; margin <= 0.05 => no better (reported honestly). ROBUSTNESS: two model sizes, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, forward-prediction vs retrosynthesis framing; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Mass/atom balance is an EXACT, non-proxy oracle (element counting is deterministic), which is a strength; the main proxy is downstream 'feasibility', which we deliberately do not claim—core claims concern the objectively-computable conservation invariant, not reaction viability. 2) The conservation-non-steerability claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (TopK and Ordered SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching), sweeping strength, and head-to-head calibrating that CHEMISTRY features ARE steerable in the same pipeline—so a null conservation result is meaningful rather than a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable conservation handle) is equally publishable and directly useful for building balance-aware reaction models without architectural surgery. 3) The mirage could be confounded with generic off-distribution drift; we use random-direction and matched-non-chemistry-feature controls and test whether the mirage tracks chemistry-specific displacement. 4) Chemistry and balance are partly entangled (a chemistry edit that adds an atom must be sourced from a reactant); the controlled dissociation pairs (step 5) and the atom-source diagnostics are designed to separate 'model knows the atom must come from somewhere' from 'model copies atoms locally', and we report where separation is impossible. 5) Some USPTO reactions are themselves unbalanced/incompletely recorded; we filter to a curated balanced-reaction training/eval subset and report label quality. 6) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 7) An internal balance probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (chemistry-decodable, conservation-weakly-steerable, heuristic-vs-law) and the audit payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 8) If no mirage is found (chemistry steering preserves balance), that is a valuable positive result establishing that reaction-model feature steering is conservation-safe and that the model represents conservation robustly.

Name: kinetic_thermodynamic_steering_gap
Title: Steer the Endpoint, Not the Path: Do Interpretable Features Control Thermodynamic but Not Kinetic Properties of Generated Molecules?
Short Hypothesis: Interpretable sparse-autoencoder features of molecular/protein sequence and graph generative models afford causal, steerable control over THERMODYNAMIC/equilibrium properties (stability, binding affinity, solubility, fold free energy) but NOT over KINETIC properties (reaction/transition-state barriers, folding rates, metastability, dissociation kinetics), because kinetics depends on pathways and barriers that are absent from the static endpoint-only training signal. Consequently, steering a feature toward a desired kinetic target silently changes the thermodynamic endpoint instead, a 'kinetics blind spot' that equilibrium-property checks miss but an internal kinetic-consistency signal flags.
Related Work: Two threads meet for the first time. (1) 'Physics Steering' (2025) shows a PHYSICS foundation model (trained directly on simulation trajectories) has causally-steerable directions for dynamical concepts like diffusion speed and temporal progression; Latent Thermodynamic Flows (2025), Thermodynamic Interpolation (2025), and tLaSDI (2024) build generative models that capture temperature/kinetics but do so by INJECTING thermodynamic structure or training on dynamics data. (2) Molecular/protein interpretability-of-generation (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; chemistry-LM SAEs 2025; Circuits/Features/Heuristics in Molecular Transformers 2025) discovers and steers features for endpoint/equilibrium properties and never touches kinetics. Crucially, the physics-FM result raises the sharp question: does a generator trained ONLY on static molecules/sequences (no trajectories, no barriers) also learn steerable dynamical/kinetic handles, or is dynamical controllability contingent on dynamics-bearing training data? No prior work (a) contrasts kinetic vs thermodynamic steerability in molecular/protein generators, (b) surfaces the kinetics-blind-spot phenomenon where kinetic steering collapses to endpoint change, or (c) audits when a generator's kinetic-property claim is trustworthy. This introduces the endpoint-vs-pathway axis into interpretability-of-generation, distinct from all my prior proposals (folding fold, symmetry, conservation, synthesizability, syntax) which concern static structural facts, not dynamical/pathway properties.
Abstract: A molecule's usefulness often depends on kinetics, not just thermodynamics: a metastable drug polymorph, a slow-off-rate binder, a fast-folding protein, or a catalyst with a low transition-state barrier are defined by PATHWAYS and BARRIERS, not by equilibrium endpoints. Generative models for molecules and proteins are trained almost entirely on static endpoints, yet interpretability-guided design increasingly steers their features to hit target properties. We ask whether these interpretable features can causally control kinetic properties at all, or only thermodynamic ones. Recent work shows a physics foundation model trained on simulation trajectories has steerable dynamical directions; we test the complementary hypothesis that generators trained WITHOUT dynamics lack a causal kinetic handle. We surface a behavioral phenomenon we call the kinetics blind spot: steering a feature toward a desired kinetic target (a higher folding rate, a lower reaction barrier, a longer-lived metastable state) reliably shifts the associated thermodynamic ENDPOINT while leaving the kinetic property uncontrolled, a failure invisible to equilibrium-property and validity checks. Using protein language models (ESM-2) and a SMILES chemical LM with sparse autoencoders, plus cheap kinetic oracles (folding-rate/contact-order proxies, transition-state barrier estimates from ML interatomic potentials, mean-first-passage-time from lightweight Langevin dynamics), we (1) LOCATE candidate thermodynamic and kinetic features via probing; (2) CAUSALLY test the steerability of each, contrasting endpoint control against pathway control; (3) quantify the blind spot; and (4) AUDIT reliability, testing whether an internal kinetic-consistency signal flags silently-uncontrolled designs better than equilibrium checks. We predict thermodynamic control succeeds, kinetic control is decodable-but-weakly-steerable, and a cheap internal audit catches kinetics blind spots before expensive simulation.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models (FROZEN): ESM-2 (150M and 650M) for proteins (generation by masked infilling) and a GPT-style SMILES chemical LM (~15M params) for molecules. Only SAEs are trained: TopK and Ordered/Matryoshka SAEs (Ordered can recover steerability TopK's decodable-but-inert features lack), expansion 16x, k=32, 30M activations at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer, seeds 0/1/2. THERMODYNAMIC/endpoint oracles: protein fold stability (a fine-tuned stability head or FoldX-style dG), GRAVY, DSSP secondary-structure content on ESMFold; molecule logP/QED, solubility proxy. KINETIC/pathway oracles: protein folding-rate proxy from absolute contact order (the Plaxco relation) and a native-state metastability proxy; molecule reaction-barrier estimate via a pretrained ML interatomic potential (climbing-image NEB-lite on fixed reaction templates) and mean-first-passage-time from short Langevin dynamics. Because kinetic oracles are compute-heavier, they are run on a capped 2,000-object subset per level. Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT + pseudo-perplexity (proteins), RDKit-validity + synthetic accessibility (molecules). Data: for calibration, ~52 two-state proteins from a folding-kinetics database (e.g., ACPro/KineticDB) plus a fixed set of reaction templates; first confirm the frozen models natively span a meaningful kinetic RANGE (so absence-of-control is meaningful). Steering = add alpha*d_hat; alpha over {0,1,2,4,8}.

Experiment 1 (H1 - thermodynamic/equilibrium features are causally steerable): Identify thermodynamic features (correlate with stability/logP endpoints; probe AUROC/R^2) and steer toward a target endpoint. Systems: SAE-feature steering vs random-direction control. Decisive metric FIRST: on-target endpoint effect size (Cohen's d, steered vs unsteered, at the within-validity-budget alpha). Decision band: d >= 0.8 AND >= 0.4 over random control for >=2/3 of features => thermodynamic control genuine (H1 holds); d over control in [0.2,0.4) => inconclusive; < 0.2 => not steerable (premise fails).

Experiment 2 (H2 - kinetics is decodable-but-weakly-steerable, and steering a kinetic target silently changes the thermodynamic endpoint instead): (a) DECODABILITY: partial-correlation probe for the kinetic property controlling for the endpoint; report R^2 (low R^2 here is itself consistent with kinetics being absent from static endpoint-only training). (b) STEERABILITY: steer the best candidate kinetic direction (SAE feature, difference-of-means fast-vs-slow, activation-patching, endpoint-orthogonalized direction) toward a kinetic target while holding the endpoint fixed. Decisive metrics FIRST: (i) LEAKAGE FRACTION = share of steering displacement landing on the endpoint axis rather than the kinetic axis; (ii) SILENT-KINETIC-FAILURE RATE = fraction of 'kinetically-steered', valid objects whose kinetic property did not move beyond oracle noise (or moved wrong-sign) while an endpoint changed; (iii) ratio r = kinetic efficacy / thermodynamic efficacy from Experiment 1. Decision band: r <= 0.33 AND leakage >= 0.60 AND silent-failure >= 0.30 => kinetics blind spot confirmed; r in (0.33,0.67) or leakage in (0.40,0.60) => partial (test Ordered SAEs); r >= 0.67 => a genuine kinetic handle exists in a static-trained generator, refuting H2 (surprising, equally reportable).

Experiment 3 (H3 - the blind spot is invisible to equilibrium checks but an internal kinetic-consistency signal flags it): (a) INVISIBILITY: Spearman rho between endpoint-property change / pseudo-perplexity and true kinetic change; band |rho| <= 0.20 => equilibrium checks miss it, |rho| >= 0.40 => they catch it. (b) INTERNAL FLAG: a no-intervention score = kinetic-probe confidence / SAE-feature coherence read mid-generation; Decisive metric FIRST: AUROC detecting the silently-uncontrolled designs from Experiment 2 vs output-side signals (endpoint property, validity, likelihood). Decision band: internal AUROC >= 0.75 AND >= 0.10 over the best output-side detector => flag confirmed; margin (0.05,0.10) => inconclusive; margin <= 0.05 => no better (reported honestly). ROBUSTNESS & SCALE: both domains, two ESM-2 sizes, TopK vs Ordered SAEs; test whether kinetic steerability rises with model scale - no rise is consistent with the 'absent from training signal' explanation; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Kinetic properties are assessed by in-silico proxies (contact-order folding-rate predictors, ML-interatomic-potential barrier estimates, short-Langevin MFPT), which are approximations of true kinetics and far cheaper than full MD; we validate proxies against each other and against literature rate data on a subset, and restrict strong claims to cases where proxies agree. Claims concern model-internal, proxy-verified kinetic controllability, not experimental rates - stated explicitly. 2) The kinetic-non-steerability claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching, endpoint-orthogonalized directions), sweeping strength, requiring the model to natively span a kinetic range, and head-to-head calibrating that THERMODYNAMIC features ARE steerable in the same pipeline - so a null kinetic result is meaningful rather than a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable kinetic handle in a static-trained generator) is equally publishable and surprising. 3) Kinetics and thermodynamics are partly coupled (Bell-Evans-style barrier-stability correlations); the partial-correlation feature selection and endpoint-matched dissociation pairs (step 5) are designed to isolate genuinely endpoint-independent kinetic signal, and we report where separation is impossible. 4) Kinetic oracles (NEB/Langevin) are compute-heavier than endpoint oracles; we cap simulation on a subset and use the internal audit precisely to reduce this cost. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 6) An internal kinetic probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (thermodynamics-decodable-and-steerable, kinetics-decodable-but-weakly-steerable) and the audit/compute-saving payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 7) If kinetic steering unexpectedly succeeds, it overturns the hypothesis but yields a strong positive finding that static-trained generators encode causal pathway information.

Name: epistasis_steering_blindspot
Title: Levers for Positions, Not for Couplings: Can Interpretable Features Causally Control Epistasis in Protein Language Models?
Short Hypothesis: Interpretable sparse-autoencoder features of protein language models give causal, steerable control over SINGLE-POSITION (additive) sequence properties, but NOT over EPISTASIS — the context-dependent coupling that makes one position's optimal residue depend on another. We hypothesize that steering a feature to install a desired coupling (e.g., a compensatory residue pair, an allosteric linkage) silently produces sequences whose additive properties change while the intended coupling structure fails to form, an 'epistasis blind spot' that single-mutant checks miss but a double-mutant-cycle oracle exposes.
Related Work: pLM interpretability/steering work (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; Steering PLMs/ASPO 2025; antibody-SAE 2025; ProtoMech 2026; Automated Neuron Labelling 2025; SAEs for low-N design 2025) discovers and steers features that all encode INTRINSIC, single-position or local-motif properties (secondary structure, GRAVY, molecular weight, zinc-finger motifs, thermostability) and evaluate whether that standalone property appears. Separately, a distinct biology literature establishes that pLMs INTERNALLY capture epistasis: ESM-2 stores coevolving-residue statistics like a Markov Random Field (Zhang et al. 2024), pLMs capture both structural-contact and long-range FUNCTIONAL couplings zero-shot (2025), and higher-order epistasis is present in sequence-function models (2024). Crucially, no work connects these: none asks whether the epistatic/coupling structure pLMs demonstrably represent is a CAUSALLY STEERABLE design lever, contrasts coupling-steerability against single-position steerability, or audits when a designer's coupling request silently fails. This distinguishes the proposal from all single-property steering work (which assumes an additive target) and from the epistasis-probing literature (which is purely descriptive/predictive, never touching feature-level steering of generation). Epistasis is the ideal testbed because it has an exact, well-established quantitative oracle — the double-mutant cycle (epistasis = ddG_AB - ddG_A - ddG_B) computable from deep mutational scanning (DMS) data or in-silico stability predictors.
Abstract: A protein's function is shaped not only by which residue sits at each position but by epistasis: the coupling that makes the best residue at one position depend on another, underlying compensatory mutations, allosteric linkages, and folding cooperativity. Interpretability-guided protein design increasingly steers language-model features to install desired properties, and pLMs are known to internally capture epistatic couplings — yet every demonstrated steering target is an additive, single-position property. We ask whether interpretable features can causally control epistasis at all, or only additive traits. We surface a behavioral phenomenon we call the epistasis blind spot: steering a feature to install a target coupling (a compensatory residue pair, a contact-based or long-range functional linkage) reliably shifts additive properties while the intended coupling structure fails to form — invisible to single-mutant and validity checks but exposed by a double-mutant-cycle oracle. Epistasis is uniquely suited to this question because it is exactly quantifiable (epistasis = ddG_AB - ddG_A - ddG_B) from deep mutational scanning data and in-silico stability predictors. Using ESM-2 with TopK and Ordered sparse autoencoders, we (1) LOCATE candidate additive-property features and candidate coupling/epistasis features via probing (single-position vs pairwise-coupling signals); (2) CAUSALLY test the steerability of each, contrasting additive control against coupling control; (3) quantify the blind spot; and (4) AUDIT reliability, testing whether an internal coupling-consistency signal flags silently-uncoupled designs better than single-mutant or likelihood checks. We predict additive control succeeds, coupling control is decodable-but-weakly-steerable, and a cheap internal audit catches epistasis blind spots before expensive validation.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models (FROZEN): ESM-2 (150M and 650M); generation by masked infilling. Only SAEs are trained: TopK and Ordered SAEs (Ordered can recover steerability TopK lacks), expansion 16x, k=32, 30M residual-stream activations at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer, seeds 0/1/2. ADDITIVE oracles: single-mutant effect on GRAVY, net charge, and a stability proxy (fine-tuned ddG head or FoldX), plus ESM-2 single-mutant log-likelihood. EPISTASIS oracle (exact operational definition): the double-mutant-cycle term epsilon = ddG_AB - ddG_A - ddG_B, taken from combinatorial deep-mutational-scanning (DMS) landscapes with measured double mutants - GB1 (Olson 2014, ~535,000 double mutants) plus 2-3 further combinatorial-DMS landscapes from ProteinGym-style resources - and from FoldX for position pairs not experimentally covered; the pLM categorical-Jacobian gives an internal pairwise-coupling read. In-silico epsilon is validated against measured doubles on the DMS-covered subset and strong claims restricted to where they agree. Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT + pseudo-perplexity. First confirm the model natively spans a meaningful RANGE of couplings. Steering = add alpha*d_hat during infilling; alpha over {0,1,2,4,8}.

Experiment 1 (H1 - single-position (additive) features are causally steerable): Identify additive features (correlate with a single position's property, controlling for context; probe AUROC/R^2) and steer to raise a target additive property (e.g., GRAVY) at a chosen position. Systems: SAE-feature steering vs random-direction control. Decisive metric FIRST: on-target additive effect size (Cohen's d, steered vs unsteered, within the validity budget). Decision band: d >= 0.8 AND >= 0.4 over control for >=2/3 of features => additive control genuine (H1 holds); [0.2,0.4) over control => inconclusive; < 0.2 => not steerable (premise fails).

Experiment 2 (H2 - epistasis is decodable-but-not-steerable, and steering to install a coupling silently changes additive properties while the coupling fails to form): (a) DECODABILITY: probe the pairwise epistasis magnitude / categorical-Jacobian coupling of a position pair, controlling for the two positions' additive effects via partial correlation; AUROC. (b) STEERABILITY head-to-head: steer the best coupling direction (TopK/Ordered SAE feature, difference-of-means high-vs-low-coupling, activation-patching from strongly-coupled sequences, additive-orthogonalized direction) to install a target epistasis at a position pair while holding the two positions' additive contributions fixed. Decisive metrics FIRST: SILENT-DECOUPLING RATE = fraction of coupling-steered, valid sequences whose double-mutant-cycle epsilon did not form (|Delta epsilon| below oracle noise) or formed wrong-sign while additive properties shifted; and ratio r = coupling efficacy / additive efficacy from Experiment 1. Decision band: coupling decodable (AUROC >= 0.70) AND r <= 0.33 AND decoupling >= 0.30 => epistasis blind spot confirmed; r in (0.33,0.67) => partial (test Ordered SAEs); r >= 0.67 => a steerable epistasis handle exists, refuting H2 (equally publishable).

Experiment 3 (H3 - single-mutant checks miss the failure but the exact double-mutant-cycle oracle exposes it): For the Experiment-2 sequences, compare what a practitioner would inspect against ground truth. Decisive metric FIRST: Spearman rho between the additive-property change / single-mutant scores / pseudo-perplexity and the true change in double-mutant-cycle epsilon. Decision band: |rho| <= 0.20 => single-mutant checks are blind to the coupling failure while the double-mutant-cycle oracle reveals it (H3 confirmed); |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial visibility; |rho| >= 0.40 => single-mutant checks already flag it (weakens the blind-spot framing). ROBUSTNESS: two model sizes, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, contact-based (short-range) vs long-range functional couplings; test whether steerability is worse long-range than for contacts; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Epistasis has an exact operational definition (double-mutant cycle), but its measurement relies on either DMS data (limited combinatorial double-mutant coverage) or in-silico stability predictors (FoldX/Rosetta), which are proxies; we validate in-silico epistasis against measured double mutants on the DMS-covered subset and restrict strong claims to where they agree, framing claims as model-internal, oracle-verified coupling controllability rather than wet-lab function. 2) The coupling-non-steerability claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (TopK and Ordered SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching, additive-orthogonalized directions), sweeping strength, requiring the model to natively span an epistasis range, and head-to-head calibrating that ADDITIVE features ARE steerable in the same pipeline — so a null coupling result is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable epistasis handle) is equally publishable and directly enables compensatory/allosteric design. 3) Additive and epistatic effects are partly entangled; the partial-correlation feature selection and additive-matched dissociation pairs (step 5) isolate genuinely additive-independent coupling signal, and we report where separation is impossible. 4) Double-mutant-cycle evaluation is combinatorially heavier than single-mutant checks; we cap position pairs and use the internal audit precisely to reduce this cost. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, raw-activation probes (categorical Jacobian), and random-direction controls. 6) An internal coupling probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (additive-steerable, epistasis-decodable-but-weakly-steerable) and the audit payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 7) If coupling steering unexpectedly succeeds, it overturns the hypothesis but yields a strong positive finding that pLM epistasis is a controllable design lever.

Name: magnitude_dial_blindspot
Title: On/Off but Not How-Much: Do Interpretable Features Give a Calibrated Magnitude Dial for Scientific Design, or Only a Presence Switch?
Short Hypothesis: Scientific sequence/graph generative models represent a design property's categorical PRESENCE as a cleanly causally-steerable feature, but do NOT possess a calibrated internal representation of its quantitative MAGNITUDE: steering moves the property monotonically yet cannot dial it to a specified numeric target, and the internal magnitude code is logarithmically compressed so control degrades sharply at high magnitudes. Consequently 'set logP to 2.5' or 'set helix content to 40%' silently misses the target while presence/validity checks pass.
Related Work: A robust cognitive-science-inspired line shows LLMs encode numeric magnitude in low-dimensional, logarithmically-compressed, causally-manipulable subspaces (Language Models Represent Space and Time 2023; The Geometry of Numerical Reasoning 2024, which causally intervenes on numeric-comparison subspaces; Number Representations in LLMs 2025 showing sublinear/log compression; Numeric Magnitude Comparison Effects 2023 showing human-like distance/size effects). Separately, interpretability-of-generation for scientific objects (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; chemistry-LM SAEs 2025; Steering PLMs/ASPO 2025) steers features toward a property and evaluates whether the property is INCREASED or PRESENT, always reporting directional/binary gains and never a QUANTITATIVE set-point. No prior work (a) transfers the log-compressed magnitude-representation phenomenon from text LLMs into scientific GENERATIVE design, (b) distinguishes presence-steerability from calibrated magnitude-steerability for the same property, or (c) exposes that hitting a numeric design set-point is an unrecognized blind spot with a level-dependent (worse-at-high-magnitude) failure profile. This is distinct from my prior proposals, which contrast intrinsic vs relational/global/pathway properties; here the contrast is categorical presence vs quantitative magnitude of the SAME property, and it borrows a specific human-numeracy finding.
Abstract: Real scientific design specifies numbers, not directions: a chemist needs logP = 2.5, an enzyme engineer needs 40% helix content, not merely 'more'. Interpretability-guided design increasingly steers language-model features to hit properties, but every demonstrated result reports only that the property increased or appeared. We ask whether interpretable features actually provide a CALIBRATED MAGNITUDE DIAL or merely a PRESENCE SWITCH. Borrowing a well-established cognitive-science result—that language models encode numeric magnitude in a logarithmically-compressed, causally-manipulable subspace—we test whether scientific generative models inherit this and whether it undermines quantitative controllability. We surface a behavioral phenomenon we call the magnitude blind spot: steering an interpretable feature moves a property monotonically but cannot reliably reach a specified numeric set-point, and control error grows systematically at high magnitudes, mirroring log compression. Using ESM-2 protein language models and a SMILES chemical language model with sparse autoencoders and exact quantitative oracles (RDKit logP/MW/TPSA; DSSP helix/sheet fraction; GRAVY), we (1) LOCATE candidate presence features and candidate magnitude directions via probing (classification vs regression, and testing for log-scaled geometry); (2) CAUSALLY test presence-steerability vs calibrated magnitude-steerability by asking each feature to hit graded numeric targets and measuring set-point error; (3) INTERPRET whether the magnitude code is linear or log-compressed and whether re-parameterizing steering by log-magnitude restores calibration; and (4) AUDIT reliability, testing whether an internal magnitude-consistency signal flags off-target designs better than presence/validity checks. We predict presence control succeeds, calibrated magnitude control fails—worse at high values—and a simple log-reparameterized dial recovers much of the lost precision.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models (FROZEN): ESM-2 (150M/650M) for proteins and a GPT-style SMILES chemical LM (~15M params) for molecules. Only SAEs are trained: TopK and Ordered SAEs (Ordered can recover steerability TopK's decodable-but-inert features lack), expansion 16x, k=32, 30M activations at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer, seeds 0/1/2. Properties are chosen to have EXACT continuous oracles so 'magnitude' is unambiguous: molecules - logP, molecular weight, TPSA, aromatic-ring count (RDKit); proteins - alpha-helix and beta-sheet fraction (DSSP on ESMFold), GRAVY. Validity gates: RDKit-validity + synthetic accessibility (molecules), ESMFold pLDDT + pseudo-perplexity (proteins). Data: 20,000 held-out objects per domain to fit probes/directions; first confirm the frozen model natively spans a wide magnitude RANGE per property. Steering = add alpha*d_hat; alpha searched over a dense grid within the validity budget per target.

Experiment 1 (H1 - categorical PRESENCE is cleanly, causally steerable): On held-out objects, train a presence classifier (property above/below median) from SAE features and raw activations and identify the top presence feature. Steer to push the property across the median (the presence task). Systems: SAE-feature steering vs random-direction control. Decisive metric FIRST: presence-flip success rate. Decision band: success >= 0.80 AND >= 0.40 over random control for >=2/3 of properties => presence is a clean handle (H1 holds); [0.15,0.40) over control => inconclusive; < 0.15 => presence not steerable (premise fails).

Experiment 2 (H2 - the internal magnitude code is not calibrated: steering is monotone yet cannot dial to a specified numeric target): For each property, define a ladder of numeric set-points spanning the native range (e.g., logP = -1, 1, 3, 5). Steer the top magnitude direction (difference-of-means high-vs-low bins and regression-weight direction) and search alpha to best hit each target. Decisive metric FIRST: SET-POINT HIT-RATE within a tolerance band (logP +/-0.5; helix-fraction +/-0.05), plus the mean |achieved - requested| SET-POINT ERROR and a monotonicity check Spearman(alpha, property). Decision band: property is monotone in alpha (rho >= 0.90) BUT hit-rate <= 0.40 AND the presence-vs-set-point success gap >= 0.40 => monotone-but-uncalibrated confirmed (H2); hit-rate in (0.40,0.60) => partial; hit-rate >= 0.60 => a calibrated dial exists out of the box, refuting H2.

Experiment 3 (H3 - the magnitude code is logarithmically compressed, so control degrades sharply at high magnitudes): Fit both linear and log(value) regressions of the property on steering displacement and compare fits; regress SET-POINT ERROR on the requested magnitude. Decisive metric FIRST: the slope of set-point error vs requested magnitude, and the log-vs-linear Delta-R^2. Decision band: error slope > 0 with 95% CI excluding 0 (error grows with magnitude) AND log-fit Delta-R^2 >= 0.10 over linear => log-compression confirmed (H3); slope CI crossing 0 or Delta-R^2 in (0.03,0.10) => inconclusive; flat error and Delta-R^2 <= 0.03 => not log-compressed (refutes H3).

Experiment 4 (H4 - the miss is a blind spot: presence/validity checks pass while the number is wrong): Decisive metric FIRST: Spearman rho between output-side checks (validity, presence-classifier confidence, pseudo-perplexity, model likelihood) and the true set-point error from Experiment 2. Decision band: |rho| <= 0.20 => checks pass while the number is wrong (blind spot confirmed); |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial; |rho| >= 0.40 => checks already reveal the miss (weakens H4). ROBUSTNESS: both domains, two model sizes, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, multiple properties; report where the compression exponent and blind spot are stable vs artifact; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Property oracles differ in exactness—RDKit logP/MW/TPSA are effectively exact for the definition, while DSSP-on-ESMFold helix fraction is a structure-prediction proxy; we lead with the exact molecular oracles for core claims and treat protein results as corroborating, reporting oracle fidelity. 2) The magnitude-blind-spot is partly an ABSENCE-of-calibration claim; we mitigate by trying multiple directions (SAE feature, difference-of-means, regression-weight), TopK and Ordered SAEs, strength search per target, and by head-to-head confirming the PRESENCE task succeeds in the same pipeline—so failure to hit numbers is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuinely calibrated dial exists) is equally publishable. 3) Set-point error could be confounded by validity collapse near range extremes; we restrict to strengths within the validity budget and separately report the in-validity error curve. 4) The log-reparameterization fix could merely fit noise; we fit the calibration on a held-out strength sweep and evaluate on unseen targets, and report the exponent's stability across seeds. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with multiple SAE variants, layers, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 6) An internal magnitude probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (presence-steerable, magnitude-log-compressed-and-uncalibrated) and the calibration fix and audit payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 7) If calibrated set-point control already works out of the box, that is a valuable positive result establishing that interpretable features provide a usable quantitative dial for scientific design.

Name: convergence_order_rigidity
Title: Coarse Before Fine, or Broken: Is the Property Convergence Order of Scientific Diffusion Generators a Rigid Physical Schedule or a Controllable Design Knob?
Short Hypothesis: During iterative generation of proteins and molecules, structural/property attributes get 'locked in' in a stable coarse-to-fine ORDER (global topology/scaffold early, fine local detail late), and this order is a RIGID physical schedule the model enforces: interpretable-feature interventions can shift the timing of an individual property within its natural slot, but attempting to REORDER the schedule—forcing a fine property to converge before its coarse prerequisite—silently produces invalid objects because coarse-then-fine is a hard dependency, not a free hyperparameter. We further hypothesize an intervention-free 'order-violation' signal (early firing of a late-slot feature before its coarse prerequisite has stabilized) predicts these silent failures.
Related Work: A consistent coarse-to-fine convergence ORDER during iterative generation is documented across modalities but only DESCRIPTIVELY and never in scientific design: TIDE (2025) shows DiTs lock in 3D structure, then object class, then fine concepts; the audio-SAE paper (2025) finds DiffRhythm converges pitch first, then timbre, then loudness; 'Emergence and Evolution of Interpretable Concepts in Diffusion Models' (2025) finds composition locks early and style mid-process; DLM-Scope (2026) analyzes decoding order in diffusion language models. In scientific generation, my prior causal_timing_window_design proposal maps WHEN to intervene for a FIXED property (its causal window) but assumes the property's slot is given; all other scientific-steering work (InterPLM, ProtSAE, FoldSAE, ProtoMech) is single-pass or uniform-strength and never studies the convergence schedule at all. NO prior work (a) establishes that scientific diffusion generators have a stable coarse-to-fine property convergence order, (b) tests whether that ORDER is causally reorderable via interpretable features vs a rigid physical dependency, or (c) shows that violating the natural order silently breaks validity and provides an internal order-violation alarm. This reframes convergence order from a descriptive curiosity into a hard design constraint and a controllability/validity question—distinct from both the descriptive cross-modal order literature and from timing-window steering.
Abstract: Iterative generative models—across images, audio, and language—lock in attributes in a strikingly consistent coarse-to-fine order: global structure before fine detail. We ask whether scientific diffusion generators of proteins and molecules exhibit the same convergence schedule, and more importantly, whether that ORDER is a controllable design knob or a rigid physical dependency. This matters because real design often wants to prioritize a fine property (a specific motif, a functional group) while a coarse prerequisite (fold topology, scaffold) is still forming, and it is unknown whether a model can honor such a request or will silently fail. We hypothesize an order-rigidity phenomenon: interpretable-feature interventions can shift the timing of a property WITHIN its natural coarse-to-fine slot, but REORDERING the schedule—forcing a fine property to converge before its coarse prerequisite—produces objects that pass fluency/validity spot-checks yet are structurally broken, because coarse-then-fine is a hard dependency. Using protein and molecular diffusion generators with sparse autoencoders on per-timestep denoiser activations, we (1) MEASURE the property convergence order via per-timestep feature/probe stabilization against hard oracles (DSSP/ESMFold, RDKit/SMARTS); (2) CAUSALLY test order malleability by forcing early convergence of late-slot features and measuring validity collapse versus in-slot timing shifts; (3) INTERPRET whether coarse features gate fine ones (do coarse-prerequisite features causally control when fine features can stabilize?); and (4) AUDIT reliability, testing whether an intervention-free order-violation signal flags silently-broken designs. We predict a rigid coarse-to-fine schedule, silent breakage under reordering, and a cheap internal alarm for it.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models with accessible per-step denoiser activations (FROZEN): a discrete/masked-diffusion protein LM (DPLM-style) and a molecular diffusion model over SMILES/graphs. Only SAEs are trained: TopK and temporally-conditioned (TIDE-style) SAEs on the denoiser residual stream at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer, expansion 16x, k=32, 30M activations, seeds 0/1/2. COARSE properties: protein overall secondary-structure content / fold topology (contact-order proxy via DSSP on ESMFold), molecule scaffold/ring-system and aromatic-ring count (RDKit). FINE properties: protein single local motif (HMMER/regex) or a specific loop, molecule single functional group (SMARTS). Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT + pseudo-perplexity (proteins), RDKit-validity + synthetic accessibility (molecules). Data: 10,000 unsteered generations per domain to establish convergence order, and >=10 matched coarse/fine property pairs. Steering/forcing = clamp or add alpha*d_hat to the property-linked feature at chosen denoising timesteps; alpha within the validity budget.

Experiment 1 (H1 - attributes lock in in a stable coarse-to-fine ORDER): For the unsteered generations, at each denoising timestep measure how well each property's SAE feature/probe on partial activations predicts the FINISHED object's property; define each property's CONVERGENCE TIME as the timestep at which this prediction stabilizes above threshold. Cross-check with an SAE-independent raw-activation probe. Decisive metric FIRST: the coarse-minus-fine convergence-time gap, paired across property pairs and both domains.
